knowledge:
- key_parameters: delta=Path length (number of edges) to look forward from the hypothesis node to observed target nodes ;; listOfNodes=An optional subset of node names to restrict hypothesis generation and ranking ;; correctPredictionsThreshold=A threshold to restrict computationally expensive significance calculations to hypotheses with at least this many correct predictions (speeds up execution) ;; useCubicAlgorithm=Boolean specifying whether to use the fast cubic approximation algorithm (default, TRUE) or the exact quartic algorithm (FALSE) ;; numberOfDeltaToScan=The maximum path length to scan when running SCAN (default is 5) ;; topNumGenes=The number of top-scoring hypotheses to keep per delta in SCAN (default is 150) ;; doParallel=Boolean to enable parallel processing across multiple cores ;; numCores=Integer specifying the number of processor cores to use when parallel processing is enabled ;; nodeInclusionFile=An optional text file containing node names to filter the network during CCG creation ;; excludeNodesInFile=Boolean specifying whether to exclude (TRUE) or include (FALSE) the nodes listed in nodeInclusionFile
- alternatives: The fast cubic approximation algorithm (useCubicAlgorithm=TRUE) is preferred for larger networks over the exact but computationally expensive quartic algorithm (useCubicAlgorithm=FALSE). SCAN (runSCANR) is preferred over single-delta analysis (RankTheHypotheses) to limit false positives by identifying regulators that consistently score highly across multiple path lengths.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a prior knowledge causal interaction network (e.g., in SIF format) and differential expression data (containing up-regulated, down-regulated, and non-differentially regulated genes) and want to identify and rank upstream regulators that explain the observed expression changes.
- pitfalls: Excluding non-differential results (0s) from the experimental dataset will lead to inaccurate significance calculations, as CausalR will treat them as unmeasured. Setting delta too high (close to or above the network's average degree) connects most hypotheses to most nodes, degrading the scoring algorithm's ability to differentiate good hypotheses from bad ones. Node names are case-sensitive.

workflows.name: standard_causal_reasoning
workflows.intent: Predict, score, and rank upstream regulators at a specific path length (delta) and calculate their statistical significance.
input: testNetwork1.sif (prior knowledge causal network in Cytoscape SIF format)
testData1.txt (two-column tab-separated experimental data containing node names and regulation values: -1, 0, or 1)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the network and construct a Computational Causal Graph (CCG) using CreateCCG.
2. Load the experimental data and map it to the CCG using ReadExperimentalData.
3. Rank all hypotheses at a specific path length (delta) using RankTheHypotheses.
4. (Optional) Generate predictions for a specific signed hypothesis using MakePredictionsFromCCG and score it using ScoreHypothesis.
5. (Optional) Calculate exact or approximate significance p-values using CalculateSignificance and enrichment p-values using CalculateEnrichmentPvalue.
6. (Optional) Export the sub-network of correctly explained nodes for a specific hypothesis to SIF format using WriteExplainedNodesToSifFile.
workflows.code:
ccg <- CreateCCG(system.file( "extdata", "testNetwork1.sif", package="CausalR"))
experimentalData <- ReadExperimentalData(system.file( "extdata", "testData1.txt", package="CausalR"),ccg)
RankTheHypotheses(ccg, experimentalData, delta=2)
predictions <- MakePredictionsFromCCG('Node0',+1,ccg,2)
ScoreHypothesis(predictions, experimentalData)
GetNodeName(ccg,CompareHypothesis(predictions, experimentalData))
Score<-ScoreHypothesis(predictions,experimentalData)
CalculateSignificance(Score, predictions, experimentalData)
PreexperimentalDataStats <- GetNumberOfPositiveAndNegativeEntries(experimentalData)
experimentalDataStats<-c(PreexperimentalDataStats,1)
predictionListStats<-AnalysePredictionsList(predictions,8)
CalculateSignificance(Score,predictionListStats, experimentalDataStats, useCubicAlgorithm=TRUE)
CalculateEnrichmentPvalue(predictions, experimentalData)
WriteExplainedNodesToSifFile("Node1", +1,ccg,experimentalData,delta=2)

workflows.name: sequential_causal_analysis_scan
workflows.intent: Run Sequential Causal Analysis of Networks (SCAN) across multiple deltas to identify robust upstream regulators and generate their explained sub-networks.
input: testNetwork1.sif (prior knowledge causal network in Cytoscape SIF format)
testData1.txt (two-column tab-separated experimental data containing node names and regulation values: -1, 0, or 1)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the network and construct a Computational Causal Graph (CCG) using CreateCCG.
2. Load the experimental data and map it to the CCG using ReadExperimentalData.
3. Run the SCAN algorithm across a range of deltas using runSCANR to find common top-scoring regulators.
4. Export the sub-networks of correctly explained nodes for all common SCAN hypotheses using WriteAllExplainedNodesToSifFile.
workflows.code:
ccg <- CreateCCG(system.file( "extdata", "testNetwork1.sif", package="CausalR"))
experimentalData <- ReadExperimentalData(system.file( "extdata", "testData1.txt", package="CausalR"),ccg)
scanResults <- runSCANR(ccg, experimentalData, numberOfDeltaToScan=2, topNumGenes=4,correctPredictionsThreshold=1, writeResultFiles = FALSE, writeNetworkFiles = "none",quiet=FALSE)
WriteAllExplainedNodesToSifFile(scanResults, ccg, experimentalData, delta=2, correctlyExplainedOnly = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
